claim: Dataset contamination artificially inflates LLM accuracy on standard multiple-choice questions, but its impact is substantially reduced when the NOTO variation is used because models cannot rely on memorized answers.
falsifier: Compare LLM accuracy on a held-out private dataset versus a public dataset in both standard and NOTO formats; the accuracy gap should be larger in the standard format.

conditions: Standard multiple-choice format vs. NOTO variation
Public datasets (e.g., MMLU) vs. private datasets
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported LLMs, datasets (MMLU, UNED-Access 2024), and zero-shot setting; transfer beyond these conditions is unestablished.

title: Dataset contamination–Accuracy inflation in standard mechanism
